title: QGenda Alternative | We Build It, You Keep QGenda
description: QGenda alternative for GME programs seeking a managed service. We deliver complete block, call and clinic schedules, built to the ACGME requirements, as Excel or Google Sheets, or on a custom live view we build for you.
h1: QGenda Manages Your Schedule. We Build It.
paragraph: Keep QGenda for the day to day. Scheduling Wizard builds the schedule you run in it, to the ACGME requirements, no migration, no software to learn.

cta.title: Ready to Stop Building Schedules Yourself?
cta.description: Book a call to talk through your scheduling needs and learn how Scheduling Wizard works. Join 30+ departments across 20+ hospitals and practices that have us build their call, block, clinic and shift schedules.

faq.answer: Scheduling Wizard replaces QGenda for schedule creation and optimization, not for schedule viewing. Many Scheduling Wizard clients continue using QGenda as their day-to-day publishing platform; they put the finished schedule Scheduling Wizard delivers into it. The key distinction is that Scheduling Wizard handles the complex work of building and optimizing the schedule, while QGenda serves as the publishing platform.
faq.question: Is Scheduling Wizard a replacement for QGenda?

faq.answer: ACGME duty hour rules are applied as the schedule is built, not checked manually after the fact. We apply the 80-hour weekly limit, eight hours off between duty periods, the 24-hour cap, and subspecialty-specific rules. The review afterwards is a check, not a repair job.
faq.question: How does Scheduling Wizard handle ACGME duty hour compliance?

faq.answer: Scheduling Wizard produces Block rotation schedules, Call schedules, Clinic schedules, and Attending schedules. All four schedule types are optimized simultaneously so that changes in one do not create conflicts in another. Finished schedules are delivered as Excel or Google Sheets, or on a custom live view we build for you that programs can upload to viewing platforms like QGenda.
faq.question: What types of schedules does Scheduling Wizard produce?

faq.answer: No. Scheduling Wizard is a managed service, not self-service software. Chief residents submit their program's rules and requirements, and the Scheduling Wizard team delivers finished schedules. There is no platform, interface, or software for chiefs to operate or learn.
faq.question: Do chief residents need to learn new software to use Scheduling Wizard?

faq.answer: The subspecialty requirements you tell us apply are built in too. During sales calls, ACGME compliance is consistently the first question program directors and chiefs ask, and specifically whether we know the rules for their subspecialty. We ask you for them, write them down with you, and build to them rather than applying generic duty hour rules across all programs.
faq.question: How does Scheduling Wizard handle subspecialty-specific ACGME rules?

faq.answer: Scheduling Wizard handles mid-year revisions including sick leave, parental leave, resident swaps, and new rules. When changes occur, affected portions of the schedule are rebuilt without disrupting the full schedule. Programs submit the updated rules and receive a revised schedule rather than rebuilding it manually.
faq.question: What happens when scheduling rules change mid-year?

hero.title: QGenda Manages Your Schedule. We Build It.
hero.description: Keep QGenda to publish and manage the day to day. Send us your block, call and clinic rules, the ACGME ones and the local ones, and we build the schedule you run in it.

items.title: Built to Your Rules, However Granular
items.description: We build to your rules and requests, however complex or granular: the written ones, including the ACGME requirements where they apply, and the local ones nobody has written down. The attending who does not take Friday call. The two residents who cannot share a rotation. The clinic that needs Thursdays protected. If you can describe it, it goes in.

items.title: Scheduling Knowledge That Persists
highlights: New chiefs start with a working system
items.description: Your program's scheduling rules, requests and configurations stay with Scheduling Wizard year over year. When your chief residents rotate, incoming chiefs inherit a working schedule instead of a blank spreadsheet.

items.title: Optimized Rotation Schedules Generated
items.description: Scheduling Wizard generates year-long block rotation schedules that respect PGY-level requirements, elective preferences, coverage minimums, and ACGME rotation mandates, fully optimized, not manually assembled.

items.title: Block, Call and Clinic Synchronized
items.description: Block, call, clinic and attending schedules are built together. A change in one propagates across the others, which removes the cascade of manual fixes.

items.description: Schedules come back in the format your program asks for, as Excel or Google Sheets, or on a custom live view we build for you. When someone goes on leave, a rotation changes or coverage shifts mid-year, we rebuild around it. Major redrafts are part of the engagement rather than a change order, which is the difference between a finished schedule and a draft you maintain.

features.title: What Scheduling Wizard Takes Off Your Plate
features.description: Scheduling Wizard handles schedule creation and optimization end-to-end so your team focuses on running the program, not operating software.

items.title: Software Still Requires Manual Work
items.description: QGenda gives you scheduling tools. Configuring the rules, building the schedule and fixing what the draft gets wrong is still your team's work.

items.title: Knowledge Lost Every Year
items.description: When chiefs rotate annually, hard-won scheduling knowledge walks out the door. New chiefs start from scratch inside complex software with no institutional memory.

items.title: Compliance Falls on Your Team
items.description: Verifying ACGME duty hour compliance in self-service software is a manual, error-prone process, and the misses only surface later.
